idiom_name: translation filter at the seam + explicit field mapping
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define one type per wire contract (source DTO, target DTO or canonical model) and one pure function or small component that maps source to target field by field, with an explicit failure path for messages that do not validate. Place it where the format changes: consume the source format from the inbound channel, publish the target format to the outbound channel, and route untranslatable messages to an invalid-message channel instead of publishing a half-translated message. Keep the mapping declarative (a table, annotations or schema mapping) where the language allows it, and translate into a canonical model rather than into each consumer as soon as more than two formats participate. The mapping must be total and explicit - no field is silently dropped - and the translator should be stateless so redelivery and retries are safe.
code_sketch:
translate(message):
    src = parse(SOURCE_SCHEMA, message.body)        # validate before mapping
    dst = SOURCE_TO_TARGET.map(src)                 # explicit field/unit/encoding rules
    publish(OUTBOUND_CHANNEL, encode(TARGET_SCHEMA, dst))
# failures -> INVALID_MESSAGE_CHANNEL; never publish a half-translated message
pitfalls: Mapping format pairs directly makes the number of translators grow with the square of the formats; insert a canonical model once more than two formats participate.
A translator that silently drops unmappable fields corrupts the semantics without failing anything.
Without an invalid-message path a failed translation either stops the whole pipeline or leaks a malformed message downstream.

Wrong move: use the translator to look up and add facts absent from the source -> the mapping becomes nondeterministic and coupled to an external service, and fails when that lookup is unavailable -> instead use a Content Enricher for external data, then keep the translator focused on schema and semantic conversion.
